mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.5% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified rising rate period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 5% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same or
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05) despite the labor indicators meeting the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected future earnings and supports higher equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate exceeds 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day log returns for SPX are not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified demand acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% while inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 3% suggests supply-side strength without price pressures, reducing growth expectations and pushing S&P 500 forward returns into negative territory over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO grows by >2% monthly and CPIAUCSL < 3% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: robust supply expansion with deflationary inflation
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative (p > 0.05) despite the supply signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 3%, it indicates a shift toward rate easing, lowering real discount rates and increasing the present value of future equity cash flows, which should produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 3%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative (p < 0.05) during the easing period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% combined with a decline in labor turnover (PAYEMS) suggests a tight labor market, which can trigger wage inflation and reduce real interest rates, pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE drops below 3.5% and PAYEMS decreases by 2% or more in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) despite the labor indicators meeting the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of accelerating consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 4% suggests a loss of monetary policy control, prompting central banks to raise rates, which compresses growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by at least 4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative (p > 0.05) during the inflation acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 3% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing demand, which can lead to earnings downgrades and a decline in equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the contraction.
